caseno: Criminal petition for leave to appeal No. 32 of 1997.
lawyer: For Petitioner: Mr. M.A. Jalil, Advocate instructed by Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record. Respondents: Not represented.
parties:
Md. Abdul Khaleq Master ----- Petitioner
Versus
Ahmed Ali and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal, J: The informant-petitioner lodged an F.I.R. on 18-1-91 alleging dacoity in the night following 17-1-91 in his house, implicating in total 31 accused persons. After investigation by the Officer-in-charge of P.S. Fulbaria and subsequently by four Inspectors of C.I.D. a charge-sheet was submitted on 12-10-93 against 5 accused persons and final report was submitted in respect of the others. On 23-10-93 the informant-petitioner filed a naraji petition before the learned Magistrate praying for a judicial inquiry by a Magistrate. By an order dated 27-4-94 the learned Magistrate accepted the naraji petition and directed further investigation by a Senior C.I.D. Officer. On 4-12-94 the informant-petitioner filed another naraji petition repeating his prayer for judicial inquiry by a Magistrate. By an order of the same date the learned Magistrate rejected the petition on the ground that the case being under investigation by higher authorities of the C.I.D., the naraji petition was not tenable. The informant-petitioner moved the learned Sessions Judge, Mymensingh under sec-tion 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, Criminal Revision No. 275 of 1994, against the said order of the learned Magistrate dated 4-12-94 and the learned Sessions Judge by his order dated 3-1-95 dismissed the revisional application on the ground that the matter being already under further investigation by the C.I.D. there was no scope for filing any naraji petition which was misconceived. Against the said order of the learned Sessions Judge dated 3-1-95 the informant-petitioner filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 317 of 1995 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the said order dated 3-1-95. By judgment and order dated 26-1-97 a Division Bench of the High Court Division discharged the Rule on the ground, first, that the informant-petitioner having not preferred any revisional application against the order of the learned Magistrate dated 27-4-94, his second naraji petition after 8 months on 4-12-94 was not maintainable and, secondly, the Miscellaneous case before the High Court Division is in fact a second revisional application in the camouflage of an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and hence the miscellaneous case is misconceived. 

 3. Mr. M.A. Jalil learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the informant-petitioner had to submit the second naraji petition after 8 months on 4-12-94 because the same C.I.D. Officials were investigating the case and it is they who had earlier submitted final report in respect of the remaining accused persons, although there were sufficient materials for including them as accused in the charge-sheet. 

 5. Mr. M.A. Jalil next submits that the petitioner's miscellaneous case was not a second revisional application in the camouflage of an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the learned Judges of the High Court Division wrongly held that it was so.
